# Verdict: REVISE ## Summary The implementation demonstrates good architectural intent by attempting to combine a high-level error summary with per-field inline feedback. However, it suffers from a major architectural collision: **dual announcement collision (Broadcast vs. Association anti-pattern)**. By combining `role="alert"` + programmatic focus on the error summary alongside four simultaneous `aria-live="polite"` regions on field errors, screen readers will experience conflicting, duplicate, or truncated announcements upon form submission. Furthermore, it lacks autocomplete attributes on standard identity fields, lacks an accessible mechanism to expose password requirements, and has color contrast / focus visibility gaps on error anchor links. --- ## Pre-commitment Predictions 1. **Double/conflicting announcements on submission**: Using live regions/alerts on *both* the summary and individual form fields will trigger an announcement storm in screen readers. 2. **Missing autocomplete attributes**: Registration forms handling email, password, and personal info typically miss `autocomplete` tokens. 3. **Password requirement timing and description**: Password length/rules are communicated only upon failure rather than proactively via `aria-describedby`. 4. **Target size or contrast issues**: Inline error messages or links inside the summary may fail text contrast thresholds. *Post-investigation result*: All 4 predicted issues are present in this fixture. --- ## Findings ### Critical Findings (Blocks Access) *None that completely trap or block users.* --- ### Major Findings (Significantly Degrades Experience) 1. **Dual Announcement Storm: Broadcast vs. Association Collision** - **Location**: `RegistrationForm.jsx:75` and `RegistrationForm.jsx:110` - **Element**: `
` in error summary + multiple `
` on individual fields - **Impacted Users**: Screen reader users (VoiceOver, NVDA, JAWS) - **WCAG / APG**: WCAG 3.3.1 (Error Identification), WCAG 4.1.3 (Status Messages), Known Anti-Pattern #1 (*Broadcast vs. Association*) - **Evidence**: ```jsx // RegistrationForm.jsx:75
... // RegistrationForm.jsx:110
``` - **Why this matters**: When the form is submitted with 4 blank fields, five separate live announcements fire simultaneously: the `role="alert"` summary AND all four `aria-live="polite"` regions. Simultaneously, `summaryRef.current?.focus()` moves focus to the summary container. Because screen reader announcement queues get clobbered, VoiceOver and NVDA will either cut off the summary announcement, speak inline errors repeatedly out of order, or speak every error twice (once via live region, once when reading the summary or tabbing to the field). - **Fix**: Choose one channel for the submit event. In the standard GOV.UK / W3C pattern, the error summary container should rely on **programmatic focus** (`tabIndex={-1}` and `.focus()`) to trigger AT reading—or use `role="alert"` *without* active inline `aria-live` regions. **Remove `aria-live="polite"` from the individual field containers (`RegistrationForm.jsx:110`).** Field errors must be associated via `aria-describedby` (Association), not broadcast via live regions (Broadcast). 2. **Missing Password Rules Proactive Association** - **Location**: `RegistrationForm.jsx:99-108` - **Element**: `` - **Impacted Users**: Cognitive accessibility users, Screen reader users - **WCAG / APG**: WCAG 3.3.2 (Labels or Instructions), WCAG 3.3.5 (Help) - **Evidence**: ```jsx // Password requires at least 8 characters, but this rule is only revealed in errs.password on failed submit: if (formData.password.length < 8) { errs.password = 'Password must be at least 8 characters.'; } ``` - **Why this matters**: Users with cognitive disabilities or screen reader users have no way of knowing the 8-character requirement until *after* submission fails. - **Fix**: Render helper text (e.g. `Must be at least 8 characters`) and associate it with the input via `aria-describedby="password-hint"` (concatenating `error-password` when invalid: `aria-describedby="error-password password-hint"`). 3. **Missing `autocomplete` Attributes on Personal Data Fields** - **Location**: `RegistrationForm.jsx:62-67`, `RegistrationForm.jsx:99-108` - **Element**: ``, ``, ``, `` - **Impacted Users**: Cognitive accessibility users, Motor-impaired users - **WCAG / APG**: WCAG 1.3.5 (Identify Input Purpose - Level AA) - **Evidence**: Inputs are rendered dynamically without `autocomplete`: ```jsx ``` - **Why this matters**: Autocomplete allows user agents and assistive technologies to autofill credentials, preventing manual cognitive strain and typing friction. - **Fix**: Add autocomplete attributes to `fieldDefs`: - `email`: `autocomplete="email"` - `password`: `autocomplete="new-password"` - `confirmPassword`: `autocomplete="new-password"` - `displayName`: `autocomplete="username"` (or `name` / `nickname`) --- ### Minor Findings (Friction but Workaround Exists) 1. **Color Contrast on Error Summary Anchor Links** - **Location**: CSS `.error-summary a { color: #dc2626; }` inside `.error-summary { background: #fef2f2; }` - **Impacted Users**: Low vision users - **WCAG / APG**: WCAG 1.4.3 (Contrast - Minimum) - **Evidence**: `#dc2626` text on `#fef2f2` background yields a contrast ratio of **4.48:1**, which narrowly fails the WCAG AA minimum requirement of **4.5:1** for regular (16px) body text. - **Fix**: Darken link color to `#b91c1c` (contrast ratio 6.04:1) or `#991b1b` (contrast ratio 8.24:1). 2. **In-Page Anchor Jump Does Not Explicitly Move Focus** - **Location**: `RegistrationForm.jsx:83` (``) - **Impacted Users**: Keyboard-only users - **WCAG / APG**: WCAG 2.4.3 (Focus Order) - **Evidence**: The summary links use standard HTML hash links ``. While browsers scroll to ``, some browser/screen reader combinations do not automatically move keyboard focus to the input unless clicked with a mouse or handled via scripted focus. - **Fix**: Add an `onClick` handler or ensure the link handler calls `.focus()` directly on the target input element: ```jsx { e.preventDefault(); document.getElementById(`field-${field}`)?.focus(); }}> ``` --- ### Enhancements (Best Practice Not Met) - **Submit Button State During Processing**: If submission is asynchronous, add `aria-busy="true"` and disable the submit button while pending. - **Heading Hierarchy**: The component renders `

Create your account

` and `

There are X errors...

`. Ensure that when embedded into an application layout, `

` does not conflict with page-level headings. - **Show/Hide Password**: Provide an accessible toggle button (`aria-label="Show password"`, `aria-pressed="false"`) so users can verify input before submitting. --- ## What's Missing - **Missing Proactive Password Constraints**: No helper text associated via `aria-describedby` before error generation. - **Missing Autocomplete Specifications**: Violates WCAG 1.3.5 for user identity and credential fields. - **Missing Synchronized Focus on Error Links**: Standard in-page hash links on single-page React forms frequently fail to transfer keyboard focus across all browsers. --- ## Multi-Perspective Notes - **Screen Reader User**: Severe risk of announcement conflicts on submit due to `role="alert"` on the summary firing at the exact same moment as four inline `aria-live="polite"` regions. Once inline `aria-live` is removed, the combination of `tabIndex={-1}` programmatic focus on the summary and `aria-describedby` on invalid inputs creates a clean, standard experience. - **Keyboard-Only User**: Focus is successfully moved to the summary on submit (`summaryRef.current?.focus()`), and focus indicators are clearly visible with offset rings. However, clicking the error anchor links may not reliably transfer keyboard focus directly into the invalid input field in all user agents without an explicit `.focus()` event. - **Low Vision User**: Visual hierarchy is clear with red borders and backgrounds. However, the text color `#dc2626` on `#fef2f2` sits right below the 4.5:1 threshold (4.48:1), making error links harder to read under reduced contrast or sunlight. - **Cognitive Accessibility**: Password length rules are hidden until the user makes a mistake. Adding visible helper text associated via `aria-describedby` and enabling browser `autocomplete` significantly reduces cognitive burden. ### Perspective Alarm Levels | Perspective | Alarm Level | Trigger Signal | |-------------|-------------|----------------| | Screen reader | **HIGH** | Dual announcement storm (`role="alert"` + multi-field `aria-live="polite"`) | | Keyboard-only | **MEDIUM** | In-page error hash link focus movement across browsers | | Low vision | **MEDIUM** | Borderline color contrast on error links (4.48:1 vs 4.5:1) | | Cognitive | **HIGH** | Hidden password constraints, missing `autocomplete` attributes | | Vestibular & motion | **LOW** | No motion or animation present | | Auditory access | **LOW** | No audio or video media present | | Environmental contrast | **MEDIUM** | `#dc2626` on `#fef2f2` contrast compliance | --- ## Verdict Justification The verdict is **REVISE**. While the component implements visible focus states, form labels, `aria-invalid`, and summary focus shift, it falls squarely into the known **Broadcast vs. Association anti-pattern** by broadcasting both the summary and individual field updates through active live regions simultaneously. Removing `aria-live="polite"` from the field wrappers, adding `autocomplete` tokens, providing proactive password instruction associations, and correcting link contrast will elevate this implementation to an **ACCEPT**.
